newsitem.title: USA: LDC debt rises after Fed stays pat, Brazil recoups.
newsitem.headline: LDC debt rises after Fed stays pat, Brazil recoups.

text.p: Emerging debt prices gained Wednesday after the Federal Reserve opted to leave U.S. interest rates steady and a short-covering rally pushed Brazilian paper higher, traders said.
The emerging debt market had little energy overall, as players awaited confirmation of expectations the Fed would maintain a steady policy.
Steady U.S. rates would likely prolong the fund flow into emerging market debt, which posted strong returns this year.
"Seeing the U.S. Treasuries trading so rich, it forces people to look at us," one Brady bond trader said.
The U.S. T-bond closed 4/32 lower for a yield of 6.45 percent.

Brazilian debt bounced back as market players became accustomed to expectations that the country's would post a poor trade perfomance in October, even as Brazilia announced it would not release the data until next week.
"Brazil had a nice bounce back today," said one emerging market investor said. "A lot of people had shorted the Brazilian Bradies and now they have been covering."
Brazilian Cs gained 3/4 to 70-1/2, while the country's pars picked up 1/4 to 60-1/4.
"Yesterday was a day of widening and today was a day of catching up," the trader added. "On a relative value Brazil started looking attractive."
The debt market has priced in an Brazil's October deficit at $1.0 billion, but uncertainty over the data would likely continue to keep the market captivated, analysts said.

"The big question remains Brazil at this point," said one strategist at a U.S. bank. "I'm not sure you're going to see a quick resolution between people who are a little worried and those who think the process is moving in the right direction."
Brasilia announced Wednesday it would postpone release of the trade data until next week.
Elsewhere, Argentine FRBs rose 1/2 to 84 bid and Mexico's 2026 global slipped 3/8 to 102-1/4.
Wall Street players were eagerly awaiting Russia's Eurobond launch. Several traders said did not expect the deal to price until December.

"A lot of the real investors have pulled their horns in just aren't intersted in doing anything," another Brady trader said. "They are looking at the Russian global. Their attention isn't really on Latin America."
Russia dollar-denominated Vnesh loan gained 1/4 to 79-5/8 bid.
